title: The Shadow Factory at Nuffield Theatre - review
transcript: how Brenton's an inspired choice to launch the Nuffield Southampton's new theater space his new play the shadow factory is not only about the city in the second world war it's an epic drama that fills this large new space virtually the only elements of a fantastic set designed by 59 Productions tubular lights above that bend and move to recreate brilliantly the sense of planes overhead a Maps projected on the floor of the thrust stage to show not only the scene locations but the targets are German bombs one such target is the main factory producing Spitfires once this is blown up production switches to multiple locations in the area the shadow factory of the title and this is where it gets interesting the British government once at war committed to full-on war without mercy or conscience in this play we see them requisitioning property specifically a local audre business and a country house with no care for the owners the central characters are there to give a human face of the story but not I suspect distractors by tugging at the heartstrings even so the excellent casts do bring them to life in special mention here for Anita Dobson and David Berle playing to vivid characters each a chorus of local people appear regularly and by the device of singing together create a strong sense of community in the face of German bombardment and government dictatorship some Hajus production of the shadow factory hits the target and I give it four stars you
